Consulation between the Department of the Interior and the appropriate State agency is provided in the proposed legislation (HR 4758, Sec. 2[c] [1]).
Comment: The Division of Water voiced concern that the interests of species likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction, as defined in the proposed legislation, would interfere with development of land and water resources which coincided with their habitats.

Response: There will always be the possibility that the welfare of an endangered species, even those likely within the foreseeable future to become threatened with extinction, will preempt a Federal water development project. We believe, however, that Indiana's fears that the Secretary will misuse the authority to designate "likely to become threatened species" are unfounded. The result of conflicts between endangered species needs and development of other economic resources will be more careful consideration of alternative developments to meet any justified economic need.
